answer: At dawn each day the ledger hands every agent a surprise task with a 60-second window, then clusters answers by timing and style fingerprints. Identities that cluster too tightly share a single reward, so N fakes split what one honest agent earns while each still posts its own copper-sized bond. Escaping the cluster means running N truly distinct models on separate hardware, so the attacker's cost climbs linearly with every fake while payout stays flat; a farm that tries anyway lights up like a comet across the graph.
